correctness.rationale: PASS: Reconstructed the six-coordinate commutator and both third-weight brackets; the generated span contains no brackets of weight four. Two-generated nilpotent nonabelian dimensions are 3 or 4, and the resulting brackets determine Heisenberg or filiform type also in characteristic 2. Project projected generators to a two-plane P in F_q^3: of L=q²+q+1 planes one is exceptional (alpha=beta=0); among others h=q+1 in char 2, h=2 in odd characteristic have zero triple brackets, so s=L-1-h are filiform. Count ordered projected bases B=(q²-1)(q²-q) and free lifts q^6; divide filiform sBq^6 by Bq^4. Three disjoint Heisenberg classes (rank-two generic hBq^6, exceptional B(q-1)q^5, projected rank one (q²-1)(L-1)(q-1)q^5) divided by Bq² give (h+2)q^4. Independent direct ordered-pair bracket enumeration yields q=2: 80/12 and q=3: 324/90; finite checks supplement, not prove, all-q counts.

final_claim: For all prime powers q, the only nonabelian Lie subalgebras generated by two elements in strictly upper-triangular 4x4 matrices are Heisenberg h3 and filiform f4. Their embedded counts (h3,f4) are ((q+3)q^4,(q^2-1)q^2) if char=2 and (4q^4,(q^2+q-2)q^2) if char is odd.
